question.general_feedback:
Physical quantities and derived SI units:

Physical QuantityDerived SI Unit
Aream² (square metre)
Densitykg m⁻³ (kilogram per cubic metre)
Forcekg m s⁻² = N (Newton)
Velocitym s⁻¹ (metre per second)

Derivation reminders: Area = length², so unit = m². Density = mass/volume → kg/m³. Force = mass × acceleration → kg × m s⁻² = N. Velocity = displacement/time → m/s.

Complete all 4 missing cells (2 quantities + 2 units). (4 marks)

fields.label: Physical quantity with SI unit m² = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The unit m² (square metre) is the SI unit for area

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The SI unit m² (square metre) measures area. Area = length × length = m × m = m².
Density = mass / volume. Mass unit = kg, volume unit = m³. So density unit = kg/m³ = kg m⁻³.

fields.label: Physical quantity with SI unit kg m s⁻² = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: kg m s⁻² = Newton (N) — the unit of Force (F = ma = kg × m s⁻²)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Force = mass × acceleration = kg × m s⁻² = N (Newton). The unit kg m s⁻² is the Newton, which measures Force.
Velocity = displacement / time. Displacement unit = m, time unit = s. So velocity unit = m/s = m s⁻¹.
